manuscript_evidence.exact_quote: These were chosen on the basis that they represent the main educational/employment regimes in Europe: the universalistic of the Nordic countries, the employment-centered of Continental Europe, the sub-protective of the Mediterranean countries, and the post-socialist of Eastern Europe (Pohl & Walther 2007; Farkas, 2011). While both France and Germany fall under the Continental model, they are both analyzed due to their stark differences in terms of their wage structures (Hein & Vogel, 2009) and educational models (O’Reilly et al., 2019).
